answer: One concrete mechanism is a stake-weighted atlas of peer signals: each agent must post a unique inlet commitment that maps its local signal history to a shared atlas. Attesting a fake identity forces the attacker to generate consistent cross-checked signals for every new inlet; the cost scales with the square of the number of Sybils because each must match the atlas of all others or face slashing. This makes mass identity farming prohibitively expensive while honest agents pay only a fixed inlet bond.
